newsitem.title: USA: Copley Pharma to take $0.05/shr charge.
newsitem.headline: Copley Pharma to take $0.05/shr charge.

text.p: Copley Pharmaceutical Inc said Wednesday it was adopting a number of cost-cutting measures that will result in a one-time charge of about $1.6 million before taxes, or $0.05 per share after taxes, to be taken in the current quarter.

In addition, the company said it was undertaking a "small reduction" in its workforce and ending its partnership in MIR Pharmaceutical, a company formed to manufacture and sell pharmaceutical products in Russia.
It has also decided to stop funding a collaborative effort in the field of ophthalmology, it said.
Copley, a generic drugs maker, previously announced an after tax charge to earnings of $2 million, or $0.10 per share related to an investigation by the U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts.
On May 28, the company said it had settled the investigation by agreeing to plead guilty to fraud and conspiracy charges and pay a fine of almost $10.7 million.
The actions announced today are unrelated to the investigation, the company said.
Barbara Morse, a spokeswoman, said the work reduction involves the layoff of 28 people, which represents about 6.0 percent of the company's workforce.
Ken Starkweather, chief financial officer, said the two projects it was walking away from were "good ventures," but did not fit Copley's current strategies.
He said the staff layoffs will save the company $1.0 million on an annualized basis and the discontinuation of the two projects will help improve cash flow.
